about: Disease information shown with leaf-model results (docs/24 §6). Short paraphrases of the cited extension pages; every entry has a source (see SOURCES.md). Healthy classes have no entry. Chemical advice is deliberately general: the app never gives products or doses and refers the user to a local extension officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra.
general_note: This is advice, not a diagnosis. Confirm with an extension officer or Krishi Vigyan Kendra before spraying; use only products registered for the crop, at the label dose.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple black rot
manage: Remove mummified fruit from the tree and the ground

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar apple rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae); needs juniper/red cedar as a second host
manage: Remove nearby red cedar / juniper hosts where practical

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry powdery mildew
manage: Improve air flow through the canopy

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus greening (HLB)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter spp.), spread by citrus psyllids
manage: No cure: remove and destroy infected trees

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato early blight
manage: Protective fungicide sprays as advised locally

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato late blight
manage: Destroy infected tubers and volunteer plants
Fungicide sprays from emergence in risky weather, as advised locally

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash powdery mildew
manage: Plant in sun with good air flow; avoid overcrowding

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry leaf scorch
manage: Grow resistant varieties and renew plantings
Good drainage; remove old foliage after harvest

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato bacterial spot
manage: Water at the base, not over the leaves

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato early blight
manage: Fungicide at the first sign of disease, as advised locally

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato late blight
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Green patches on leaf margins turn brown, purplish-brown, then black

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-spotted spider mite (pest, not a disease)
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Brown, yellow or white stippling on leaves, later bronzing and leaf drop
manage: Soaps/oils or miticides with rotated modes of action, as advised locally

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Yellowing between veins and at the edges of young leaves; crumpled, curled leaves
manage: No cure: remove and destroy infected plants
Grow resistant varieties; use clean transplants
Monitor whiteflies with yellow sticky traps; reflective mulch
Insecticides with rotated modes of action, as advised locally

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus (ToMV), spread by hands, tools, infected seed
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling of leaves, sometimes distortion and yellowing
manage: No cure: remove and burn infected plants
Disinfect tools and wash hands between plants
